body:
I think you might need to add the keyword `dict` at the end of the line of the function definition? Does that change anything?

See: `:help Dictionary-function`

It's certainly odd to be redefining script-scoped functions/variables every time a function is called.  Does it help if you change all the `s:blink` to `blink`?

> I think you might need to add the keyword dict at the end of the line of the function definition?

That's [implied](https://vi.stackexchange.com/a/12747/15) by using the `function dict.funcname` syntax.
:+1: That's right. Forgot about that part.

I don't understand. I knew about the `dict` attribute, and I remember having tested it. It didn't change anything, and as @jamessan explained, it should be implied by the `dict.func` syntax. And yet, I've just tested it again, and now it seems to work. I've made so many tests on this bug, on so many versions of neovim that my memory must have failed.

Also, I've tried to replace `s:blink` with `blink`, but I was afraid of having a name conflict with the main function `Blink()`, so I moved the latter in the script scope `s:Blink()`. But I still get the errors and the crash.

I agree with you, the imbrication of functions is odd. I'm using my own [plugin](https://github.com/lacygoill/vim-search), with a similar blinking, but without the imbrication. It seems to work fine in Vim and Neovim.

I just wanted to report the crash, because I've begun using Neovim today, and I'm trying to understand the differences between it and Vim.

Thank you very much for your help @jamessan  and @tjdevries .

In fact `dict` solves the issue with this mapping:

    nno  n  n:call Blink()<cr>

But it fails with these mappings:

    nmap          n              n<plug>(blink)
    nno   <expr>  <plug>(blink)  Blink()

Just to be clear, this is the change I was suggesting:

```diff
diff --git a/test.vim b/test.vim
index ae3f29e..9c4b99d 100644
--- a/test.vim
+++ b/test.vim
@@ -1,9 +1,9 @@
 nno  n  n:call Blink()<cr>
 
 fu! Blink() abort
-    let s:blink = { 'ticks': 4, 'delay': 50 }
+    let blink = { 'ticks': 4, 'delay': 50 }
 
-    fu! s:blink.tick(_) abort
+    fu! blink.tick(_) abort
         let self.ticks -= 1
         let active = self.ticks > 0
 
@@ -17,7 +17,7 @@ fu! Blink() abort
         endif
     endfu
 
-    fu! s:blink.clear() abort
+    fu! blink.clear() abort
         if exists('w:blink_id')
             call matchdelete(w:blink_id)
             unlet w:blink_id
@@ -25,7 +25,7 @@ fu! Blink() abort
         endif
     endfu
 
-    call s:blink.clear()
-    call s:blink.tick(0)
+    call blink.clear()
+    call blink.tick(0)
     return ''
 endfu
```

There's no worry about a name conflict since `Blink` != `blink`.

The `dict` attribute definitely isn't needed for these functions.  If that's affecting the behavior, then it's a bug.  Maybe it will provide some insight into the behavior you're seeing.

Ok, I've just done the replacement, like in the diff you've written, and the bug is still there. In fact, it's even worse, because now, even the combination `dict` + `nno  n  n:call Blink()<cr>` fails.

So, it seems the bug is a combination of 4 factors:

  - an imbrication of dictionary functions
  - no `dict` attribute
  - a script local dictionary
  - a 2 part mapping

The mapping doesn't matter.  You can get the same behavior by manually running `:call Blink()` fast enough.

The `dict` attribute is irrelevant.  Adding that still causes ASAN to trigger.

A script-local dictionary is irrelevant.  Changing all the `s:blink` to `blink` causes ASAN to trigger.

It's looks like it's just related to variable lifetimes and timers.
